decisions.name: Sec. 2 exercises: regularity of O(r) and regularity in short exact sequences
decisions.reason: These are consistency exercises stating no result the packet promises; the exact-sequence direction is absorbed into the long-exact-sequence steps of the two regularity items.
decisions.evidence: Stands as an additional result, not as permission to omit necessary exercise implications. Current regularity-propagation steps2.1–4.1 prove all needed vanishing/generation/multiplication; uniform-regularity-fixed-polynomial F2 and steps3.1–4.1 use published explicit twisting-sheaf cohomology for O and twists, and the long exact sequence to pass from a regular kernel and source to its quotient. decisions.name: Sec. 2 Lemmes 2.5 and 2.6: bounded quotient modules and coefficient minorations
decisions.reason: These lemmas serve only the printed esquisse of the boundedness theorem; the packet's direct regularity induction replaces that route, so they are recorded as history rather than built.
decisions.evidence: Stands. Fresh Bourbaki221 PDF pages8–11 Lemmes2.5–2.6 concern leading-coefficient boundedness/minoration and limited families, using finite projection, determinants, and reduced-support families inside the expressly named boundedness esquisse. Current uniform-regularity-fixed-polynomial steps1.1–4.1 instead give a complete hyperplane induction: regular hyperplane avoiding both associated sets, sharp higher-cohomology range, strict decrease of positive H1 until zero, bound B=max(0,p*binom(n+a,n)-Q(a)), and R=a+B+1. The companion dimension-independent item steps1.1–2.1 cancels the ambient term and gives b(P). These bounds, followed by projective-space-construction steps1.1–3.1, supply the actual fixed-polynomial Hilbert construction. No coefficient-minoration theorem is used or promised; the historical sketches do not substitute for the local complete induction.

decisions.reason: The fixed-map Noetherian section-comparison argument is proved inline in universal-flattening steps 1.1 and 3.1 from a two-term twist presentation and Serre vanishing. For its universal arbitrary-test direction, step 4.1 uses the complete uniform-sections-after-flat-pullback theorem, whose cutoff depends only on the presentation and fibre polynomial, not on the test morphism. decisions.evidence: Stands with a precise correction to the original never-needed rationale. Fresh Nitsure pp.13–14 Lemma3.1 proves eventual section base change for a fixed morphism of Noetherian schemes by a twist presentation and two Serre-vanishing kernels; its cutoff may depend on that map. Current universal-flattening step1.1 explicitly reproduces this argument for its finitely many reduced partition maps, and step3.1 for the fixed Noetherian map S_P→S. Its arbitrary-test converse step4.1 instead invokes the complete uniform-sections-after-flat-pullback steps1.1–3.1, with base-flat pullback, fixed fibre polynomial, two finitely presented flat kernels and one N independent of B, including non-Noetherian B. No missing general lemma or map-dependent bound is silently used to certify all tests.

decisions.name: Sec. 1: the Quot functor for coherent quotients of a finite sum of twists
decisions.reason: The commissioned AG-MOD-1 contract is the Hilbert functor of embedded closed subschemes; general coherent quotients of a finite sum are not promised on this page and the packet deliberately fixes E = O_X.
decisions.evidence: Stands. Fresh Nitsure Section1 pp.3–4 defines general coherent Quot families E_T→F with flat proper-support F and kernel-based equivalence; Hilb is its E=O_X special case. The binding AG-MOD-1 design row commissions the Hilbert functor of embedded closed finitely presented flat subschemes, representability, universal family, polynomial strata and all base changes. The actual Hilbert Definition and main theorem preserve that contract on all test schemes and locally Noetherian bases. Auxiliary regularity of coherent quotients and the relative Grassmannian of finite module quotients are proved locally for the Hilbert construction; they do not assert representability of the general coherent-sheaf Quot functor on X. None of the26 manifest claims adds such an assertion. General Quot representability is therefore not an unmet promised result.

decisions.name: Sec. 2 Lemme 2.4: Chow-coordinate boundedness of reduced subschemes of bounded degree
decisions.reason: The Chow-coordinate route to boundedness is not used: the packet proves the uniform regularity bound directly by hyperplane induction, so this key lemma is recorded as the historical alternative.
decisions.evidence: Stands. Fresh Bourbaki221 PDF page8 Lemme2.4 explicitly bounds reduced equidimensional fibre subschemes by degree using the useful content of Chow coordinates, and is named a key input to the following boundedness sketch. Current uniform-regularity-fixed-polynomial steps1.1–4.1 and dimension-independent-regularity steps1.1–2.1 give complete recursive regularity bounds directly for fixed Hilbert polynomial, including nonreduced quotients. Projective-space-construction chooses one such degree and reconstructs every flat ideal by evaluation in steps1.1–3.1; its flattening prerequisite is fully scheme theoretic. This supplies the boundedness actually required by AG-MOD-1 without invoking Chow coordinates or a family bounded solely by reduced degree. The latter stronger/different intermediate theorem is not commissioned.

decisions.evidence: Stands for the A page. Fresh V25 pp.781–782 §28.4.4/Exercise28.4.E gives arithmetic-genus descent for reduced projective curves over a field, using the finite normalization sequence and affine O-connected⇒isomorphism. It cannot establish the commissioned arbitrary Noetherian regular-surface theorem with finite normalization assumed. Current intrinsic-regularization steps2.1–3.1 instead strictly increases coherent subalgebras inside the fixed finite normalization and applies global Noetherian ACC; embedded-SNC steps4.1–5.1 separately lower the maximum finite contact order and eliminate triple points. The finite affine implication beta_*O=O⇒beta isomorphism is proved in the strict-growth argument via affine coordinate algebras, so even the relevant exercise specialization is closed locally. Numerical field examples retain their exact delta proof. No genus, Stein-factorization or projective-field assumption is imported into the general theorem.

boundary_repairs.evidence: Step 2.1: u=0 corresponds to the zero map alpha:Q→O_S, whose image ideal is zero; therefore V(u)=S and every S-scheme factors through it.
Step 1.1: if a representing perfect complex has only its degree-zero term, then K_j^1=0, Q_j=(K_j^0)^vee, and Hom(Q_j,B)=K_j^0 tensor B directly; the same zero-locus construction in step 2.1 applies.

The homomorphism-vanishing Statement has no interval, ordered parameter, degree cutoff, or numerical endpoint. The affine opens used to glue V(u) in step 2.1 are scheme charts rather than endpoints of a numeric range.

Step 2.1 identifies u_T with the pullback of alpha:Q→O_S. If u_T=0, that map is zero on every affine open of T, so the image ideal defining V(u) maps to zero in O_T. The closed-immersion factorization criterion then gives T→V(u); this is a scheme-theoretic implication for arbitrary, including nonreduced, T.

Step 2.1 defines V(u) by the image ideal of alpha:Q→O_S. If T→S factors through V(u), its extended image ideal is zero, so alpha_T is zero. The natural Hom(Q,B) identification from steps 1.1 and 2.1 then gives u_T=0 on affine opens, hence globally. This proves the reverse implication on all test schemes.
